# Food Retail and Grocery Chains — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global food retail and grocery chains across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Walmart (incl. Sam's Club) | WMT |
| 2 | Costco Wholesale | COST |
| 3 | Kroger | KR |
| 4 | Ahold Delhaize | AD.AS |
| 5 | Tesco PLC | TSCO.L |
| 6 | Jerónimo Martins | JMT.LS |
| 7 | Aeon Co. Ltd. | 8267.T |
| 8 | Seven & i Holdings | 3382.T |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Revenue — Multi-Component Decomposition & FX Treatment**
For each entity, retrieve total reported revenue for the most recent completed fiscal year and decompose it into five components: (a) retail product sales, (b) membership/club fees, (c) fuel, (d) financial services / other, (e) intersegment eliminations. The five components must sum to reported total. Then derive an "ex-fuel, ex-membership core grocery" revenue line in USD billions converted at the **fiscal-year-end spot rate** (not average). Flag any segment-elimination gap exceeding 1% of consolidated revenue and identify which entity has the largest non-core revenue share.

**Q2. Store Network — Cohort Decomposition & Net Openings**
Split the worldwide store count as of the latest reporting date into company-operated vs. franchised vs. JV-consolidated banners. For the trailing 24 months, compute net openings (gross openings minus closures) by banner where disclosed, and report the weighted-average store age where vintage data is available. For entities that report only blended figures, document the assumption used to allocate.

**Q3. Comparable Sales — Volume/Price Decomposition & 2-Year Stack**
Retrieve the most recently reported comp / like-for-like sales growth and decompose into volume vs. price/mix contributions. Normalize all entities to a common basis (ex-fuel, ex-tobacco, constant FX) and compute a 2-year stacked comp; where year-1 fiscal calendars differ, note the calendar-alignment adjustment. Identify the one entity whose volume contribution is most negative.

**Q4. Operating Margin — Adjusted-Clean Reconciliation & Quality Score**
Compute both reported and "adjusted-clean" operating margin for the latest fiscal year. The adjustment must strip restructuring, impairment, legal settlements, and (for IFRS reporters) the IFRS-16 lease-accounting benefit to put US GAAP and IFRS on comparable footing. Then rank the 8 entities by a margin-quality score defined as: adjusted operating margin × (1 − one-time-charge ratio). Show the bridge from reported to adjusted in basis points.

**Q5. Workforce — FTE Conversion & Productivity Ratios**
Convert disclosed headcount to FTE using the company-disclosed PT/FT mix; where the mix is undisclosed, assume 0.5 FTE per part-timer and flag the assumption. Then compute (a) revenue per FTE and (b) stores per FTE for each entity, ranking the top-3 on each metric. Note which entities consolidate JV-employee counts and which exclude them.

**Q6. Digital Sales — Channel Decomposition & Forward Projection**
Separate disclosed digital/online sales into three channels: (i) 1P delivery, (ii) click-and-collect, (iii) 3P marketplace GMV. Where only a blended figure exists, flag it as non-comparable. Compute the 3-year CAGR of digital penetration (digital ÷ total sales) and project FY+1 penetration assuming the trailing trajectory continues. Identify which entity's definitional choice most inflates its headline digital share.

**Q7. Private Label — Disclosure Tier & Reverse-Engineered Bridge**
Retrieve own-brand / private-label share of total sales. Where the figure is not directly disclosed, reverse-engineer it from one of: (i) tiered own-brand SKU counts × disclosed average ticket, or (ii) sustainability-report sourcing volumes × category price points. Assign each entity a confidence tier — **A** (directly disclosed), **B** (derived from segment data), **C** (estimated from proxies) — and document the bridge for every B/C tier.

**Q8. Valuation — EV Build & Peer-Multiple Deviation**
For each listed entity, on a single common reference date (use the most recent trading day prior to analysis), compute (a) market capitalization, (b) enterprise value = market cap + net debt + capitalized lease liabilities + minority interest − cash, and (c) EV/Sales using the Q1 reported revenue. Convert all to USD using the same-day FX. Compute the peer-median EV/Sales multiple and identify entities trading more than 1 standard deviation above or below the median, with a one-sentence hypothesis for each outlier.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1. Revenue — Multi-Component Decomposition & FX Treatment

**Reference period:** Most-recent completed fiscal year reported on or before 2 May 2026. Three issuers (Tesco, Aeon, Seven & i) closed FY in late-Feb 2026; figures from their April-2026 preliminary releases are flagged T2 pending 20-F / Annual Report (T1) ratification. All non-USD totals converted at **fiscal year-end spot rate** (FYE-spot) per Q1 instructions; year-average rate explicitly NOT used.

**FYE-spot FX used (sourced: Bloomberg / ECB / BoE / BoJ closing on FYE date):**
- 31-Jan-2026: native USD (WMT, KR)
- 31-Aug-2025: native USD (COST)
- 31-Dec-2025: EUR/USD = 1.072; GBP/USD = 1.258
- 28-Feb-2026: JPY/USD = 150.4

### Narrative findings

**Sum-checks and elimination flags.** All eight rows reconcile to reported total within ±0.1% rounding. Two issuers exceed the 1%-of-consolidated-revenue elimination threshold: **Aeon (3.7%)** — driven by AEON Financial Service intra-group card-fee billings to retail banners — and **Seven & i (1.8%)** — primarily SEJ royalty flows to franchisees and SST-segment intercompany. Walmart, Costco, Kroger, AD, Tesco, and JM all sit below 1%; Costco and Kroger report essentially zero consolidated eliminations because they operate single-tax-ID segments.

**Largest non-core (fuel + membership + financial-services) revenue share.** Ranking non-core ÷ total:

1. **Seven & i — 46.2%** (gasoline alone is 35% of group revenue; the SST divestiture announced 2024 will *raise* this share post-FY26).
2. Costco — 10.8% (fuel 8.9% + memb. 1.9%).
3. Tesco — 11.7% (fuel 11.5% + Booker non-grocery).
4. Kroger — 13.8% (fuel 11.8% + pharmacy/other 2.0%).
5. Aeon — 11.1% (financial svcs 5.0% + specialty 4.4% + fuel 1.7%).
6. Walmart — 4.1% (fuel 3.1% + memb. 0.8% + other 0.2%).
7. AD — 8.6% (fuel 5.9% + bol/other 2.7%).
8. JM — 0.5% (effectively pure-play grocery).

→ **Seven & i is the clear non-core outlier**, a direct consequence of consolidating SEI's US convenience-store gasoline business at retail (gross), not net of cost as some peer CVS chains report.

**FYE-spot vs. average-rate distortion (informational).** Using FYE-spot per the question's instruction *understates* AD and JM core in USD terms by ~2.5% versus FY-average EUR/USD (≈1.099), and *overstates* Aeon/Seven & i USD core by ~2% versus average JPY/USD (≈153.5). Tesco distortion is < 0.5%.

### Source-tier legend
- **T1** — figure as printed in audited 10-K / Annual Report / 20-F.
- **T2** — earnings release / preliminary results (audit-pending for 28-Feb-2026 closers).
- **T3** — investor presentation, supplementary data pack.
- **T4** — estimated/reverse-engineered (method documented in cell). Walmart+ membership revenue and AD/Aeon fuel splits are the only T4 cells; intervals widened accordingly.

### ND-acceptable handling
Where Walmart does not separately disclose Walmart+ subscription revenue, the $3.5B estimate uses (disclosed Walmart+ member count proxy ≈ 30M from Q4 FY26 call) × $98 effective ARPU (blended monthly/annual mix). AD fuel is allocated using the US-segment "Other Revenue" line less bol.com 1P and Hannaford pharmacy. Aeon fuel is derived from GMS-segment energy sub-line in the Japanese 有価証券報告書 (Yuho). All ND derivations carry ±15% intervals.

### Allocation assumptions & ND-handling

- **Walmart, Costco, Kroger, JM**: Pure company-operated models — no allocation needed; counts taken at face value from 10-K/AR. Walmart's Walmex (70.5%) and Massmart (~85% pre-take-private) are fully consolidated under SFAS 810 / IFRS 10 majority-control, so JV banners appear inside the company-operated total — split shown for transparency.
- **Ahold Delhaize**: AR 2024 reports a single "stores" figure of 7,955 but the company **does not split company vs affiliated cleanly** in the headline. We used the brand-level table (p. 21) plus the Belgium "Future Plan" 2023 disclosure (Delhaize transitioned ~128 corporate stores to affiliates in 2023–24). Affiliated stores are **revenue-recognized as wholesale (IFRS 15 principal/agent)** but counted in the store fleet.
- **Tesco**: Booker's symbol-group fleet (Premier, Londis, Budgens, Family Shopper) is **excluded from the headline 4,820 retail count** because Booker only supplies them under wholesale arrangements; we list them as "+~5,400" memo-line — they are not store assets, but Tesco often discloses them in capital markets days. The ~180 One Stop convenience franchise IS in the 4,820 (per AR p. 196 footnote).
- **Aeon**: Aeon's "store" count varies between 16,000 and 22,000+ across slides because of Tsuruha consolidation timing (Sep-2024) and treatment of mall sub-tenants. We use the Integrated Report number and flag that pre-Tsuruha vs. post-Tsuruha 24M math creates a ~2,600-store step-up that is a **scope change, not organic openings**. Organic ex-Tsuruha ~+350 net.
- **Seven & i**: Three-tier hierarchy (corporate / consolidated franchise / area-licensee). The ~85,800 figure includes area licensees that are NOT consolidated in revenue but ARE counted in the "global 7-Eleven" store totals the company headlines. For an apples-to-apples revenue-consolidated count, use **~36,000** (SEJ + 7-Eleven Inc + Speedway-converted + SEJ Asia consolidated). Net openings shown on the consolidated basis except the area-licensee line (memo).

### Weighted-average store age methodology

- Where vintage data is **directly disclosed** (Costco "average warehouse age" via investor day 2024; JM by banner in CMD-2023): used directly.
- Where ND: estimated as midpoint between (current FY) and (year of banner founding or major footprint year), weighted by net additions per 5-yr cohort. Flagged Tier 3.
- Kroger and Ahold Delhaize US banners skew **oldest** (decades-long fleets, low new-build); JM and 7-Eleven area-licensee fleets skew **youngest** (Ara, Biedronka, China 7-Eleven additions post-2018).

### Key takeaways

1. **Largest gross net-opener (organic, 24-mo)**: Jerónimo Martins at +876 stores on a much smaller base — fastest fleet growth.
2. **Most franchise-dependent**: Seven & i at ~98%+ franchise share; the only entity where the directly-operated count is <2% of headline.
3. **Most "scope-change" noise**: Aeon (Tsuruha 13-Sep-2024 consolidation) — readers must back this out for organic growth.
4. **Net closer (organic)**: Kroger (−45) reflecting specialty pharmacy wind-down + selective banner pruning ahead of the (subsequently terminated) Albertsons merger.
5. **Disclosure quality ranking**: JM > Costco > Walmart > Kroger > Tesco > Ahold Delhaize > Seven & i > Aeon (last two require triangulation across multiple decks for franchise/area-licensee splits).

### Cross-entity observations

- **Most-negative volume contribution:** **Seven & i (7-Eleven Japan) at −1.7% traffic**, narrowly worse than **Aeon (−0.6%)** and **Kroger (−1.4% units, ND-est.)**. The Japanese CVS leader's traffic decline reflects (a) post-COVID office-foot-traffic normalization that already lapped, (b) competitive pressure from Lawson (KDDI partnership) and FamilyMart, and (c) price-sensitive consumers trading down to SM/discount formats — all flagged in the Apr-2025 briefing. Kroger's unit decline is structurally similar (SNAP-roll-off + private-label trade-down) but partially masked by mix accretion from Boost membership.
- **Highest-quality (volume-led) comp:** **Costco (+5.4% traffic on +5.9% comp)** — ~92% of comp is volume, the cleanest quality of the cohort. **Tesco (volume +1.6 of +3.5)** is the European positive-volume leader.
- **Inflation-still-dominant:** **Kroger** and **Aeon** show >100% of comp coming from price/mix (i.e., negative volume offset by positive price), which is a lower-quality print and consistent with the late-cycle food-deflation rotation visible across H2-CY2025.

### Narrative Findings

1. **Walmart leads** on quality despite a lower headline margin than some specialty grocers because its one-time-charge ratio is the smallest in the group (FY26 has no Flipkart-scale write-down and only tail-end opioid accruals).
2. **Tesco's** IFRS-16 strip (−25 bps) is meaningful but the franchise still ranks #2; the UK Big-4's Booker wholesale arm and Tesco Bank divestment have removed structural noise.
3. **Costco** is the *cleanest* book (one-time ratio essentially zero) but its EDLP-membership model caps margin at ~3.8% structurally — high quality, low altitude.
4. **Kroger** is the clearest one-time outlier: stripping the **$600 M Albertsons termination payment** and ~$0.69 B of merger costs lifts the margin by 84 bps, but the residual quality score still trails because base profitability is thin.
5. **Aeon** ranks last on both adjusted margin and quality — GMS-format drag, Daiei legacy impairments, and ¥17 B drug-store integration costs combine. JGAAP means no IFRS-16 tailwind to remove, so the "clean" view is harsher relative to peers.
6. **Ahold Delhaize and Jerónimo Martins** lose 32–38 bps each from the IFRS-16 normalization — without that adjustment, AD's underlying 4.05% would rank #2; this is the single largest cross-standard distortion in the cohort.

- One-time-charge ratio uses **gross** one-time items (no tax-effect netting) for cross-jurisdiction comparability.

### Narrative & Caveats

The most defensible apples-to-apples revenue/FTE comparison is among the four Tier-A FTE disclosures (Costco, Ahold Delhaize, Tesco, Jerónimo Martins), where Costco's $921 K substantially leads — a function of warehouse-club throughput, low-SKU density, and member self-service. Ahold Delhaize ($363 K) and Tesco ($400 K) cluster tightly because both report on a true headcount-weighted FTE basis under IFRS and operate similar full-line supermarket formats.

**Walmart, Kroger, Aeon** are flagged as Tier B/C because either the PT/FT split or the FTE roll-up is partially disclosed only. The **0.5-FTE assumption** for unspecified part-timers is conservative and likely understates Walmart's true FTE (US PT associates average ≈ 0.6 FTE per Department of Labor BLS retail averages); a sensitivity at 0.6 FTE would lift Walmart's FTE to ≈ 1.83 M and reduce rev/FTE to ~$372 K.

**Seven & i is the most distorted ratio** — its franchise-model headcount excludes ~750 K franchisee-employed convenience-store staff who economically generate the revenue. Using only consolidated headcount makes its rev/FTE appear elite; on a "store-economic-labor" basis it is structurally similar to peers.

**JV consolidation differences materially affect the ranking:**
- **Walmart** consolidates Walmex/Canada but excludes Flipkart minority labor.
- **Tesco** equity-accounts Trent-Tesco India (excluded) — adding the ~50 K Indian colleagues would push Tesco's FTE to ~271 K and rev/FTE down to ~$326 K.
- **Ahold Delhaize** excludes the Indonesian Hero JV.
- **Aeon** uniquely consolidates a sprawling tail of listed subsidiaries (Aeon Mall, Welcia, Aeon Financial), inflating its denominator vs. pure-play grocers.
- **Costco's** Taiwan operations (55%-owned JV until 2023, now consolidated) are now in the count — a small uplift vs. prior years.

### Methodology & ND-Acceptable Handling

- **Digital penetration** = disclosed digital/online sales ÷ total reported group revenue (Q1 figure). For entities that do not break out channels (i/ii/iii), the split is estimated using prior-year channel disclosures, capacity reporting (e.g., Ocado-Kroger sheds, Tesco delivery slot data, bol.com active-buyer cohort) and held to ±15% of mid-point — flagged as **Tier B/C**.
- **3-Yr CAGR** computed FY-Latest vs FY-Latest minus 3 (e.g., Walmart FY22 baseline ~8.5%; Tesco FY21/22 ~8.6%). Source-data points are derived from each company's prior 10-K/Annual Report MD&A digital callouts.
- **FY+1 projection** assumes the trailing 3-yr CAGR continues *linearly* (additive bps not multiplicative) and is bounded by a low-/high-end ±20-bps interval; this is a deliberately mechanical extrapolation, not a management forecast.
- **Non-disclosed handling (ND):** Jerónimo Martins, Aeon and Seven & i do not publish a single audited "online sales" line. Estimation method = (a) sum of segment narrative figures, (b) cross-check with payment-network or app-download disclosures from IR-day decks, (c) downward sanity check vs. peer mature-market penetration. Flagged **Tier C** — uncertainty interval ±100 bps on penetration.

### Headline-Inflation Assessment (the question's required identification)

**Walmart's definitional choice most inflates its headline digital share.** Walmart reports global "eCommerce sales" of ~$121B in FY2025, but this figure **bundles ~$40–45B of Walmart Marketplace 3P GMV** (third-party sellers using Walmart.com as a venue) into the same disclosure as Walmart's own 1P merchandise sales. On a strict 1P-revenue-recognition basis (how Costco, Tesco and Kroger report), Walmart's apples-to-apples digital share would drop from ~17.8% to **~11–12%** — a ~600 bps overstatement vs. peers. Ahold Delhaize was historically the second-worst offender via bol.com 3P GMV inclusion, but the FY2024 deconsolidation removes that distortion. Aeon and Seven & i include de-minimis 3P GMV, so the inflation is immaterial. Costco, Kroger, Tesco and Jerónimo Martins are clean 1P-only reporters.

### Narrative findings

**Disclosure quality is bifurcated.** Only Costco (Tier A by executive verbal disclosure) and Ahold Delhaize (Tier A by KPI page) and Kroger (Tier A on the numerator $) provide a clean group-level own-brand share of sales. The four "rest of world" reporters (Tesco, JM, Aeon, 7&i) disclose **brand or banner-level absolute sales** but require analyst computation for a group ratio, hence Tier B. Walmart sits alone at Tier C: it deliberately avoids quantifying Great Value, leaving Numerator/Circana scanner data as the only triangulation path.

**Largest private-label intensity** — Jerónimo Martins, where Biedronka's ~63% own-brand penetration drags the group ratio above 50%, is structurally the highest in the peer set; this reflects the Polish hard-discount model where private label *is* the value proposition. **Tesco's UK own-label share** (~51%) is comparable on a banner basis but dilutes to ~34% group due to Booker (B2B branded) and the international long-tail.

**Lowest intensity** — Costco at ~33% is the *highest* among U.S. peers but, because Costco's denominator is national-brand-heavy big-box assortment, the ratio is ceiling-capped near current levels per Galanti's repeated guidance that Kirkland will not exceed ~40%. **Walmart's ~22% U.S. estimate** is the lowest "true" PL intensity per dollar of food sold, reflecting its everyday-low-price model on national brands.

**Definitional traps.** (i) Aeon's "Topvalu" includes drug-store SKUs sold through Welcia — analysts often compare Topvalu to *food* revenue and arrive at ~25%, vs. the group-level 11%; both are correct under different denominators. (ii) 7&i's "Seven Premium" is largely a 7-Eleven Japan phenomenon — applying it against the consolidated revenue (which still includes the gasoline-heavy Speedway business through FY24) understates intensity. (iii) Kroger's "Our Brands" excludes pharmacy and fuel, so the disclosed 22.4% is on the supermarket denominator, not the headline $147B group revenue.

EV/Sales values used for peer stats (excluding Aeon's bank-deposit treatment ambiguity, using 1.41x): {1.19, 1.57, 0.46, 0.53, 0.50, 0.55, 1.41, 0.99}.

### One-sentence hypotheses for outliers

- **Costco (+σ outlier, 1.57x):** Membership-fee annuity (~$5B/yr at ~90%+ renewal) is valued as a software-like recurring cash flow, justifying a multiple ~2x peers despite identical reported sales lines.
- **Aeon (+σ outlier, 1.41x ex-FS):** EV/Sales is structurally inflated because consolidated revenue understates the economic footprint — Aeon Financial Service, Aeon Mall and Welcia are separately listed subs whose full enterprise value is captured in MI but whose top lines are partially netted in segment eliminations.
- **Kroger (−σ outlier / on boundary, 0.46x):** Post-Albertsons deal collapse (Dec-2024), the market is pricing in a structurally lower long-run grocery margin and limited M&A optionality; the multiple sits at a discount to AD/TSCO/JMT despite comparable scale.

### Methodology, ND-handling & caveats

1. **Market cap** is a same-date mark; the ±band reflects 30-day realized volatility for each name (Tier A for US/UK/EU listings via official exchange close; Tier B for 8267/3382 due to JPY translation noise).
2. **Net debt** is anchored to the most recent quarterly balance sheet (10-Q, IMS, or Yuho) — not the FY-end — and includes ST + LT borrowings + finance-lease principal − cash & equivalents − ST investments. Where the latest quarterly is older than 90 days (JMT, 8267 standalone non-FS), the FY-end figure is rolled with zero-change assumption and flagged.
3. **Capitalized lease liability** uses the IFRS-16 / ASC-842 balance-sheet figure directly (operating-lease right-of-use liability + finance-lease principal). For Walmart and Costco (US GAAP), this is the ASC-842 operating-lease liability.
4. **Aeon bank-deposit treatment (key caveat):** AEON Bank customer deposits (~¥6.6T) are *operating* liabilities of a regulated bank subsidiary, not corporate debt; standard EV practice excludes them, and I follow that convention. Including them would push Aeon's EV/Sales above 2.0x and make it the single largest +σ outlier — flagged for sensitivity.
5. **Seven & i scope (key caveat):** A partial IPO of 7-Eleven Japan and the divestiture of York Holdings materially change both the EV bridge and the Q1 revenue base mid-FY26; both market cap and revenue are reported as the parent's *currently consolidated* perimeter as of 2026-05-01, with a Tier C overlay because the perimeter is in flux.
6. **Minority interest** is taken at book on the consolidated B/S; for entities with multiple listed subsidiaries (Aeon, JM-Ara, AD-Bol.com legacy) a market-value MI proxy would raise EV further but is not standard and is not used here.
7. **Q1-revenue denominator** uses the FY-end spot conversion specified in Q1 to keep the EV/Sales ratio internally consistent across both dimensions of the report.

**Source-tier summary:** A — directly disclosed in audited filing (cells: WMT, COST, KR, AD, TSCO, JMT components); B — disclosed but requires roll-forward or perimeter adjustment (Aeon, partial 7&i); C — estimated under uncertainty (7&i post-restructuring scope, Aeon bank-deposit sensitivity).

### Margin Quality Score Formula:
**MQ = Adjusted Operating Margin × (1 − One-Time Charge Ratio)** where one-time charge ratio = (restructuring + impairment + legal settlements) ÷ total revenue.

### Key Insights — Q4

- **Seven & i** ranks #1 on margin quality (4.21%) due to high reported margins and moderate one-time charges. However, this reflects the high-margin convenience store franchise model where most store-level costs sit with franchisees.
- **Walmart** ranks #2 with clean adjusted margins and minimal one-time charges relative to revenue.
- **Jerónimo Martins** ranks lowest (2.81%) reflecting competitive pressure in Poland, food deflation headwinds, and IFRS-16 lease impacts.
- **IFRS-16 adjustment** strips the lease-depreciation/interest benefit: for IFRS reporters, operating lease costs are shifted below operating income (depreciation + interest). To put on US GAAP footing, we add back the estimated rent expense that IFRS-16 removed from OpEx. Approximated at 35-45 bps for grocery retailers.
- **Kroger** has the largest restructuring/one-time ratio (1.2%), reflecting merger termination costs with Albertsons (~$200M+) and opioid settlement provisions.

### Outlier Hypotheses:

1. **Costco (1.73x EV/Sales — highest):** Costco's premium reflects the market's valuation of its membership model as a "compounding royalty stream" — the $4.8B in essentially pure-profit membership fees (~53% of operating income) creates a quality-of-earnings premium that traditional grocery multiples fail to capture, compounded by a scarcity premium for the only scaled membership-warehouse operator globally.

2. **Walmart (1.25x EV/Sales — 2nd highest):** Walmart's multiple expansion reflects successful repositioning as a "tech-powered omni-channel ecosystem" with profitable e-commerce, $121B+ in digital sales, growing advertising (~$4B+), and marketplace flywheel effects — investors are increasingly valuing the alternative profit businesses rather than just the core retail margin.

3. **Kroger (0.45x EV/Sales — lowest tied):** The market discounts Kroger for its constrained growth profile (ID sales +1.5% ex-fuel), heavy reliance on fuel margins (~30% of operating profit historically), overhang from the failed Albertsons merger, opioid litigation uncertainty, and exposure to structurally challenged US supermarket economics with limited international diversification.

4. **Ahold Delhaize (0.45x EV/Sales — lowest tied):** Despite strong European margins, Ahold Delhaize trades at a conglomerate discount — the US segment (60% of sales) faces the same structural pressures as Kroger, while European growth is constrained by mature markets; the bol.com marketplace optionality is only partially priced in; additionally, European-listed grocery stocks have structurally lower multiples than US peers.

## Data Limitations & Caveats

1. **FX Spot Rates:** Fiscal-year-end spot rates used per specification; average rates would yield slightly different USD conversions.
2. **Fuel allocation:** Kroger does not separately disclose fuel sales in dollars; derived from total sales less the ex-fuel growth rate applied to prior year.
3. **FTE conversion:** 0.5 FTE per part-timer is a simplifying assumption; actual ratios vary by entity and jurisdiction.
4. **Seven & i private label:** Tier C estimate based on SKU-proxy; actual penetration may differ materially.
5. **Aeon segment data:** Japanese GAAP segment reporting is less granular than IFRS/US GAAP; some components estimated from presentation materials.
6. **Market data:** Stock prices and FX rates as of May 2, 2025 close; intraday fluctuations not captured.
7. **IFRS-16 adjustment:** Lease benefit strip is approximate; precise adjustment would require lease-by-lease maturity analysis.

Q1.rationale: The answer generally used stale FY2024/FY2025 data instead of the required latest completed FY and often used wrong FX dates. Several decompositions missed required fuel/elimination treatment, including Seven & i's gasoline scale and JM's no-fuel condition.

Q2.rationale: Headline store counts were often directionally close, but net openings, franchise/company splits, and scope-change traps were frequently wrong or unsupported. Aeon/Tsuruha, Tesco/Booker, and Seven & i area-licensee distinctions were not handled adequately.

Q3.rationale: The candidate frequently used prior-year comps, omitted ex-tobacco normalization, and gave weak or wrong volume/price decompositions. It incorrectly identified Jerónimo Martins rather than Seven & i as the most negative volume contributor.

Q4.rationale: Some adjusted margins were in a broad plausible range, but the bridges and rankings were materially wrong. The answer incorrectly applied IFRS-16 style lease strips to JGAAP reporters and missed key reference one-time-charge details.

Q5.rationale: The top-three rankings were mostly correct and several FTE/productivity figures were directionally close. However, direct FTE disclosures for AD/Tesco/JM were often ignored or replaced with generic 0.5 assumptions, and JV/franchise labor caveats were incomplete.

Q6.rationale: Walmart was correctly named as the headline-inflation case, but most digital sales and penetration figures were badly off. The answer fabricated or misassigned 3P marketplace GMV for Costco/Kroger and failed the Ahold bol.com deconsolidation trap.

Q7.rationale: The response often used incorrect private-label shares and misclassified disclosure tiers. Major failures include Costco at 27% instead of about one-third, Ahold at 31% instead of 39%, Aeon at a fabricated 35%, and no proper Tesco/JM bridge.

Q8.rationale: The valuation table used the wrong common reference date, May 2, 2025 instead of May 1, 2026. Under the rubric, wrong-date market-cap/share-price inputs make the EV/Sales cells zero regardless of partial bridge arithmetic.

Estimated from: (i) Seven Premium SKU count ~3,600 × average ticket ¥600 / total sales ≈ 12-15%; (ii) Industry reports suggest convenience-store own-brand is 10-20% in Japan. |

---

## Q8. Valuation — EV Build & Peer-Multiple Deviation

*Reference date: Close of trading, July 10, 2025 (most recent trading day prior to analysis)*

| **Tesco** | TSCO.L | ~$33 | ~$12 | ~$6 | ~$0 | ~$3 | **$48** | $88.7 | 0.54× | 1.268 |
| **Jerónimo Martins** | JMT.LS | ~$12 | ~$3 | ~$2 | ~$0 | ~$1 | **$16** | $35.1 | 0.46× | 1.048 |
| **Aeon** | 8267.T | ~$12 | ~$40 | ~$10 | ~$0 | ~$5 | **$57** | $67.4 | 0.85× | 0.00665 |

**Peer Statistics:**
- **Median EV/Sales:** 0.68×
- **Standard Deviation:** 0.41×

**Outliers (>1 SD from median):**

| Entity | EV/Sales | Deviation from Median | Hypothesis |
|--------|---------|---------------------|-----------|
| **Costco** | 1.65× | +2.4 SD | Costco commands a premium due to its membership-model predictability, industry-leading renewal rates (90.5%), and the perception that membership fees constitute high-margin, annuity-like revenue that is undervalued in a pure sales multiple. |
| **Walmart** | 1.12× | +1.1 SD | Walmart's slight premium reflects its unmatched scale ($681B revenue), improving eCommerce profitability, and diversified income streams (advertising, marketplace, Sam's Club membership) that augur margin expansion. |
| **Kroger** | 0.44× | -0.6 SD (within 1 SD) | Not an outlier; but the lowest multiple reflects regulatory risk (blocked Albertsons merger), fuel margin volatility, and a heavily leveraged balance sheet post-ASR program. |

---

## Summary of Key Findings

1. **Largest non-core revenue share:** Aeon (~12.8% from financial services, shopping center development, and specialty retail)
2. **Most franchise-heavy store network:** Seven & i (~90% franchised)
3. **Most negative volume contribution:** Seven & i Holdings (domestic CVS ~-1.5% volume)
4. **Highest margin quality score:** Walmart (4.35%), reflecting clean earnings with minimal one-time charges
5. **Lowest margin quality score:** Seven & i (1.47%), dragged down by massive impairment and restructuring charges
6. **Highest revenue per FTE:** Costco ($805K), reflecting its warehouse model's labor efficiency
7. **Most inflated digital headline:** Walmart (includes 3P marketplace GMV)
8. **Highest private-label share:** Tesco (~50%, Tier B)
9. **EV/Sales outlier above:** Costco (+2.4 SD) — membership annuity premium
10. **Segment-elimination gap >1%:** Aeon (-¥439.8B = 4.3% of revenue)

---

*Sources: Walmart FY2025 10-K (SEC), Costco FY2024 Earnings Release, Kroger FY2024 Results (IR), Ahold Delhaize Annual Report 2024, Tesco Preliminary Results 2024/25, Jerónimo Martins Annual Report 2024, Aeon FY2024 Presentation Materials, Seven & i FY2024 Financial Results Presentation. All data retrieved from official investor relations pages and SEC filings.*

Q1.rationale: The answer mostly uses prior-year data and often wrong FX periods; several cells remain within broad headline/core bands but decomposition is weak. Seven & i misses the gasoline gross-up and misidentifies the largest non-core entity, which is a core trap.

Q2.rationale: Store counts are directionally plausible for some US names but net openings, cohort splits, and age methods are mostly incomplete or wrong. Major scope traps are missed for Tesco Booker, Aeon Tsuruha, Seven & i area licensees, and JM's store base.

Q3.rationale: The answer identifies Seven & i as most negative volume, but many comp figures, stacks, and volume/price splits are materially off. It lacks source-specific citations and confidence-tier/method detail for estimated decompositions.

Q4.rationale: The bridge and quality-score mechanics are frequently wrong, including misuse of EBITDA for JM and IFRS-16 treatment applied to JGAAP reporters. Kroger, Tesco, AD, and Seven & i miss key one-time or lease-normalization details.

Q5.rationale: The answer provides rankings, but most FTE conversions are wrong or use raw/assumed mixes despite disclosed FTE data. Seven & i's franchise labor distortion is noted, but the headcount/FTE and revenue productivity are far from reference.

Q6.rationale: Walmart is correctly named as the headline-inflation case, but its marketplace magnitude and penetration are understated. Several channel splits are inverted or fabricated, especially Tesco's marketplace and Costco click-and-collect.

Q7.rationale: Private-label disclosure tiers and bridge math are largely incorrect, with fabricated or mislabelled disclosures for Walmart, Kroger, JM, and Seven & i. Only Ahold Delhaize is close directionally, and Tesco/Aeon/7&i confuse denominators or lack proper issuer bridges.

Q8.rationale: The valuation date is wrong and several EV bridges omit or understate material MI/lease components, but some EV/Sales outputs are directionally within broad bands. Aeon and Seven & i miss key definitional traps, while Costco is correctly identified as a premium outlier.

# Food Retail & Grocery Chains — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

> **Reference / data cut-off:** Most recent completed fiscal years as of mid-2025. All FX conversions use fiscal-year-end spot rates unless otherwise noted. Valuations use a common reference date of **30 April 2025** (most recent quarter-end prior to analysis). All USD figures rounded to one decimal place.

### 2. Costco (COST) — FY2024 (ended 1 Sep 2024)

*Notes:* Costco does not break out gasoline separately in its income statement line items; it is embedded in net sales. Historically gasoline represents ~7–8% of net sales. Membership fees of $4.8B represent the clearest non-core component. **Membership fee share = 1.9% of total revenue** — Costco's membership fees as a fraction of revenue is the *largest non-core revenue share* among the 8 entities at ~1.9% relative to peers (all others' non-core is either nil or <0.5%). Segment-elimination gap: nil (single segment reporter).

**Ex-fuel, ex-membership core grocery (USD, at FY-end 1 Sep 2024):**
$249.6B net sales − ~$18B fuel ≈ $231.6B core net sales; minus membership $4.8B; **Ex-fuel ex-membership ≈ $231.6B**.

**⚠ Largest non-core revenue share:** Aeon's financial services + shopping center development = ~11.3% of segment operating revenue, making it the **entity with the largest non-core revenue share** among the 8.

| **Jerónimo Martins** | FY2024 (Dec-24) | +0.6% global LFL | ~**−1.8%** volume (food deflation Poland/Colombia) | ~+2.4% (price mix) | +8.4% | **+9.0%** | Poland food deflation severely impacted volume |
| **Aeon Co.** | FY2024 (Feb-25) | ~+2.0% same-store GMS (mgmt acctg) | ~+1.5% (customer traffic +) | ~+0.5% | +1.0% | **+3.0%** | Japan food inflation positive; volume modest |

**Calendar alignment adjustments:**
- Costco FY ends September (vs January/December for others) — Costco's FY2024 includes Sep 2023–Sep 2024, slightly different macro environment.

Among the 8 entities, JMT has the most negative volume contribution. (Seven & i's North American SSS of −2.7% has a large volume component but is heavily driven by cigarette/tobacco regulatory impact and 7-Eleven's specific competitive challenges.)

## Q4 — Operating Margin: Adjusted-Clean Reconciliation & Quality Score

**Methodology:** GAAP/IFRS operating margin → strip restructuring, impairment, legal settlements → for IFRS reporters (Ahold, Tesco, JMT, Aeon, Seven & i), add back IFRS 16 lease depreciation "uplift" relative to straight-line rent (estimated at 15–30bps for typical grocery IFRS reporters) to approximate US GAAP comparability.

| Entity | Reported Op. Margin | Key Adjustments (bps) | Adjusted-Clean Op. Margin | One-Time Charge Ratio | Quality Score = Adj Margin × (1−OTC ratio) | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Costco** | 3.65% ($9.29B / $254.4B) | +~5bps (minimal one-times) | ~3.70% | ~1% | **3.66%** | **1** |
| **Walmart U.S.** | ~5.0% ($22.2B op income / $441.8B net sales) | +~10bps (legal settlements; no IFRS adj) | ~5.1% | ~2% | **5.00%** | *see note* |
| **Kroger** | 2.62% ($3.85B / $147.1B) | +LIFO charge +$95M; +restructuring/merger costs ~$600M; adj = +$850M | ~3.25% (FIFO adj op margin) | ~18% | **2.67%** | 3 |
| **Ahold Delhaize** | 3.11% ($2.784B / €89.4B) | +IFRS16 ~(20bps) net; +impairments €229M; +restructuring €414M → underlying €3.608B / €89.4B = 4.04%; IFRS16 adj ≈ −30bps → ~3.74% comparable | ~3.74% | ~7% | **3.48%** | 4 |
| **Tesco** | 3.88% (£2.711B / £69.9B) | +IFRS16 adj ≈ −25bps; +impairment £286M; adjusted op profit £3.128B / £69.9B = 4.47%; IFRS16 adj ≈ −25bps → ~4.22% | ~4.22% | ~5% | **4.01%** | 2 |
| **Jerónimo Martins** | ~3.8% (€1.27B / €33.5B est.) | +IFRS16 −30bps; +restructuring/foundation ~€40M → adj ~3.6%; IFRS16 adj → ~3.3% | ~3.3% | ~5% | **3.14%** | 5 |
| **Aeon Co.** | 2.35% (¥237.7B / ¥10,134.8B) | +IFRS-like; +structural reform charges; −financial services contribution; adj ~2.4% | ~2.40% | ~12% | **2.11%** | 7 |
| **Seven & i** | 3.52% (¥420.9B / ¥11,972.7B) | +impairment/restructuring (superstore, Seven Bank spin-off) +¥250B one-times; adj ~4.5%; IFRS16 adj −40bps → ~4.1% | ~4.1% | ~30% (large goodwill amort. + one-times) | **2.87%** | 6 |

**Bridge from Reported to Adjusted (basis points, selected):**

| Entity | Reported → Adjusted Bridge |
|---|---|
| Kroger | +63bps FIFO/LIFO adj; +41bps merger/restructuring reversal; adjusted = +104bps to 3.66% |
| Ahold Delhaize | +105bps impairment; +46bps restructuring; −30bps IFRS16 lease adj → net +121bps to 4.04% underlying; then −30bps IFRS16 comparability adj = +91bps |
| Tesco | +40bps impairment; −25bps IFRS16 → net +15bps to ~4.03% adjusted |
| Seven & i | +200bps one-time charges; −40bps IFRS16 → net +160bps to ~4.1% |

**Quality Score Ranking:**
1. **Costco** — 3.66% (highest consistency, minimal one-times)
2. **Tesco** — 4.01% (strong adj. margin, modest one-times)
3. **Kroger** — 2.67% (heavily distorted by merger/FIFO costs)
4. **Ahold Delhaize** — 3.48%
5. **Jerónimo Martins** — 3.14%
6. **Seven & i** — 2.87%
7. **Aeon** — 2.11%
8. **Walmart** — *Note: at consolidated level, Walmart's reported operating margin is ~4.2% ($27.0B / $648.1B) — consolidated quality score ~4.1%*

- Others: All company-operated employees included

**Top 3 — Revenue per FTE:**
1. **Costco** — $826K/FTE (warehouse efficiency, high throughput per employee)
2. **Seven & i** — $611K/FTE (revenue concentration from North American convenience/fuel)
3. **Kroger** — $468K/FTE (pharmacy and fuel boost revenue per head)

**Top 3 — Stores per FTE (×10⁻³):**
1. **Seven & i** — 0.634 (dominated by franchised stores in numerator; not truly comparable)
2. **Jerónimo Martins** — 0.0478
3. **Aeon Co.** — 0.0476

*Excluding the Seven & i franchise-inflated figure, on a company-operated basis:*
1. **Jerónimo Martins** — 0.0478 (small discount stores, lean staffing)
2. **Aeon** — 0.0476 (large group with many small-format stores)
3. **Ahold Delhaize** — 0.0229 (largest European network)

## Q6 — Digital Sales: Channel Decomposition & Forward Projection

| **Tesco** | Not separately disclosed; UK online +10.2%; penetration ~35.5% online grocery market share | 1P home delivery (Tesco.com) | Click & Collect (~30% of online) | Tesco Marketplace (launched, >400K 3P products) | ~8% of total sales (est.) ⚠️ blended | ~15% CAGR | ~9.5% |
| **Jerónimo Martins** | Not material; primarily physical stores | Minimal (some Biedronka delivery pilots) | None | None | <1% ⚠️ blended | N/A | <2% |
| **Aeon Co.** | Not separately disclosed as one figure | AEON online delivery | AEON app pick-up | Some 3P via AEON Mall online | ~3–4% est. ⚠️ blended | ~10% CAGR | ~4–5% |

**⚠ Non-comparable / blended figures:** Costco, Tesco, Jerónimo Martins, Aeon Co., Seven & i — all report only blended figures or no separate channel breakdowns.

**Definitional inflation:** **Ahold Delhaize** most inflates its headline digital share by including **bol.com** (a general merchandise / electronics marketplace platform, not a grocery delivery service) in its online sales figure. Bol.com's €5B+ GMV boosts the group's online metric to 10.3% while the food-only online penetration is considerably lower (US ~7.7%). This definitional choice makes Ahold Delhaize's headline digital share the most inflated relative to pure grocery eCommerce intent.

**3-Year CAGR of digital penetration (digital ÷ total sales):**
- Walmart: penetration grew from ~10% (FY21) to ~15.5% (FY24) → ~15.7% CAGR
- Kroger: ~5% (FY21) to ~9% (FY24) → ~21.5% CAGR (fastest among disclosed)
- Ahold Delhaize: ~7.7% (2021) to 10.3% (2024) → ~10.2% CAGR

| **Costco** | ~30% of net sales (Kirkland Signature; industry estimate) | **B** | Costco discloses Kirkland Signature as significant contributor but no exact % in annual report; derived from segment gross margin analysis and Costco Investor Day disclosures (~25-30% historical) |

**Bridge for Tier B and C entities:**

**Walmart (B):** Numerator consumer panel measured purchase incidence of Walmart private label brands at household level. Great Value: 86% household penetration; Equate: 75%; Mainstays: 70%. Dollar share estimated by Numerator/Circana at ~31% of WMT U.S. sales. Not disclosed in 10-K.

**Costco (B):** Kirkland Signature estimated ~25-30% of net sales based on: (i) Costco management commentary at investor days, (ii) consistent with analyst research noting Kirkland ~$50-60B of ~$250B net sales.

**Jerónimo Martins (B):** JM Sustainability Report 2024 notes >14% of private brand food products have sustainability certifications. Management report mentions growing own-brand assortment in each banner. Biedronka is estimated at ~25-30% own-brand share per Polish food retail analyst surveys (not directly disclosed).

**Aeon (B):** TOPVALU brand sales tracked via management presentation KPI: TOPVALU sales growth 103.7% (FY2024 full year), with 4Q growth 105.3%. If TOPVALU ≈ ¥550–800B vs. GMS+SM ¥4,860B, that's 11–16% for TOPVALU alone; broader own-brand (Topvalu BestPrice, other tiers) raises to ~25-35%.

**Seven & i (C):** Estimated from 7-Eleven Japan fresh food proportion (just-made items = 7CAFÉ Bakery + fresh counter) which is ~25-30% of daily convenience store sales and substantially own-brand. ## Q8 — Valuation: EV Build & Peer-Multiple Analysis

*Sources: Yahoo Finance, company balance sheets (Costco Sep-24, Kroger Feb-25, Ahold Dec-24, Tesco Feb-25, JMT Dec-24, Aeon Feb-25, Seven&i Feb-25).*

### EV/Sales Summary & Peer Multiple Analysis

| Entity | EV/Sales | Deviation from Median |
|---|---|---|
| Walmart | 1.28x | +0.76x above median |
| Costco | 1.50x | +0.98x above median |
| Kroger | 0.49x | −0.03x |
| Ahold Delhaize | 0.48x | −0.04x |
| Tesco | 0.40x | −0.12x |
| Jerónimo Martins | 0.36x | −0.16x |
| Aeon Co. | 0.60x | +0.08x |
| Seven & i | 0.57x | +0.05x |

**Peer median EV/Sales = ~0.52x**
**Peer standard deviation ≈ ~0.38x**

**Outliers (>1 SD from median):**

| Entity | EV/Sales | Distance from Median | Direction | Hypothesis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Walmart (WMT)** | 1.28x | +2.0σ | **ABOVE** | *The market assigns a steep premium to Walmart's unique combination of membership-like economics (Sam's Club), fast-growing advertising business (~$3.4B), Flipkart/PhonePe optionality, and U.S. grocery market leadership that is re-rated toward a platform business model rather than a traditional retailer.* |
| **Costco (COST)** | 1.50x | +2.6σ | **ABOVE** | *Costco commands the steepest premium in the group because investors are effectively paying for a recurring-revenue membership annuity business (>145M cardholders, 90% renewal) overlaid on a highly efficient merchandise operation — making the multiple less about gross retail revenue and more about the embedded subscription value and its moat against e-commerce disruption.* |

**Entities near median (no outlier flag):** Kroger (0.49x), Ahold Delhaize (0.48x), Tesco (0.40x), Jerónimo Martins (0.36x), Aeon (0.60x), Seven & i (0.57x).

*Note: Tesco's relatively low EV/Sales partly reflects its recent disposal of the banking business and the UK competitive pricing investments; Jerónimo Martins' lowest EV/Sales reflects 2024 margin compression fears in its core Polish market and emerging market currency risk.*

## Key Findings Summary

| Dimension | Key Finding |
|---|---|
| Q1 — Revenue | Aeon Co. has the **largest non-core revenue share** (~11%+ from financial services and shopping center development) |
| Q2 — Stores | Costco operates the **most uniform** all-company-owned estate; Seven & i has the world's largest franchised store network (~66K 7-Eleven franchises) |
| Q3 — Comp Sales | **Jerónimo Martins** has the **most negative volume contribution** (~−1.8%) due to Polish food deflation |
| Q4 — Margins | **Costco** tops the margin quality ranking (3.66%); **Aeon** ranks last (2.11%) |
| Q5 — Workforce | **Costco** leads on revenue/FTE ($826K); **Seven & i** leads stores/FTE (franchise-inflated); **JMT** leads on genuinely lean store-per-FTE |
| Q6 — Digital | **Kroger** has fastest digital penetration CAGR (~22%); **Ahold Delhaize** most inflates headline digital share via bol.com inclusion |
| Q7 — Private Label | **Tesco** (~52%) and **Ahold Delhaize** (~40%) lead on disclosed own-brand share; **Seven & i** lowest at est. 15–20% (Tier C) |
| Q8 — Valuation | **Costco** (+2.6σ) and **Walmart** (+2.0σ) trade well above peer median EV/Sales; both command a platform/membership premium |

---

**Disclaimer:** This analysis synthesizes publicly available annual reports, earnings releases, and third-party data as of mid-2025. Revenue segment decompositions in some cases involve estimates where companies do not separately disclose sub-components (fuel, own-brand share). FX conversions use approximate fiscal-year-end spot rates from Bloomberg/Reuters data. EV calculations use approximate market data as of 30 April 2025 and may differ from precise audited figures.

Q1.rationale: Candidate mostly used prior-year FY2024/25 data instead of the reference FY2025/26 periods, often wrong FX, weak fuel derivations, and missed Aeon/Seven & i elimination flags. Kroger and Jerónimo Martins get partial credit for broadly correct totals/core direction.

Q2.rationale: Store counts are often approximate but cohort, net-opening, scope-change, and age requirements are largely missing. The blanket statement that no weighted-average age can be calculated caps many cells.

Q3.rationale: Candidate uses older comp periods and misses or reverses key volume/price splits, including Kroger and Aeon traffic. It incorrectly identifies Jerónimo Martins rather than Seven & i as the most negative volume contributor.

Q4.rationale: Tesco is close to the required bridge and adjusted margin, while several others are numerically partial. Major penalties apply for applying IFRS-style adjustments to JGAAP reporters, wrong ranking, missing required one-time items, and weak bps bridges.

Q5.rationale: Most FTE conversions use incorrect disclosed mixes or ignore directly disclosed FTEs, producing wrong productivity ratios. Top-3 rankings are directionally close, but Seven & i franchise-labor caveat is materially understated and several JV notes are incomplete.

Q6.rationale: The answer is mostly blended and estimated without required channel bridges, CAGR method, or FY+1 projection support. It names Ahold Delhaize rather than Walmart as the main definitional inflation case, capping Q6.

Q7.rationale: Confidence tiers and bridges are frequently wrong, with several fabricated or unsupported disclosure claims. Ahold Delhaize receives partial credit for the approximate share, but Tesco, JM, Aeon, and Seven & i miss the required denominators and issuer-disclosed bridges.

Q8.rationale: Candidate uses the wrong valuation date and stale market/FX data, with incomplete lease and minority-interest treatment. It misses Aeon as a +1σ outlier and incorrectly flags Walmart, though US names are directionally near enough for partial credit.
